title_ar: تقريظ الشيخ الددو لكتاب ( شجرة الأدارسة سيدي يحيى ) للسيد الشريف الشيخ محمد المختار بن أحمد بن عبد الدائم حفظه الله
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew's Commendation of the Book The Genealogical Tree of the Idrisids of Sidi Yahya, by the Noble Sayyid Sheikh Muhammad al-Mukhtar ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Da'im, May God Preserve Him
body_ar:
قلت في تقريظ كتاب ( شجرة الأدارسة سيدي يحيى ) للسيد الشريف الشيخ محمد المختار بن أحمد بن عبد الدائم حفظه الله

محمدٌ المختار ذو العلم و الفضل

و ذو البر و الإحسان و الجود و البذل

و ذو النسب العالي الشريف و ذو التقى

و ذو الشيم المثلى و ذو الخلق السهل

قد اورثه الآباء كل فضيلة

و كمل بالأخوال فضلا على فضل

فمن آل عبد الدائم اكتسب العلى

و آل الزوين الصالحين ذوي النبل

له كتب تحوي كنوزا ثمينة

جميلة ترتيب مصححة النقل

أبان من الأنساب سفرا مفصلا

يعين ذوي الأرحام منا على الوصل

و ترجم أعلاما و حقق نسبة

و بين أوطانا و عدد للنسل

لأنساب تنواجيو يحوي مبينا

لأحفادهم فالشكل ينضم للشكل

و للقطب سيدي يحي ينهي فروعه

إلى سيِّدي إدريس ذي الشرف الأصلي

لوالده إدريس ذي المجد و العلى

إلى الندب عبد الله ذي الفضل و العدل

إلى الحسن الندب المثنى من ارتقى

ذرى العز و التوفيق و الحلم و العقل

إلى الحسن السبط ابن حيدرة الرضا

لفاطمة الزهرا إلى سيد الرسل

عليه صلاة الله تترى و آله

و أزكى سلام يجمع الفصل بالأصل

كتبه محمد الحسن بن الددو
body_en:
I said, in commendation of the book The Genealogical Tree of the Idrisids of Sidi Yahya, by the noble Sayyid, Sheikh Muhammad al-Mukhtar ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Da'im, may God preserve him:

Muhammad al-Mukhtar, possessor of knowledge and excellence,

of righteousness, kindness, generosity and open-handed giving;

possessor of a high and noble lineage, and of God-consciousness (taqwā),

of the most exemplary traits and of an easy disposition.

His forefathers bequeathed him every excellence,

and through his maternal uncles it was perfected, excellence upon excellence:

from the family of Abd al-Da'im he gained eminence,

and from the righteous family of al-Zuwayn, people of nobility.

He has books that hold precious treasures,

beautiful in their arrangement, sound in what they transmit.

He has set out from the genealogies a detailed volume

that helps those of us who are kin to keep the ties of kinship.

He has given the lives of notable figures, verified attributions of descent,

made homelands clear, and enumerated the offspring.

It holds a clear account of the genealogies of Tanwajiw

for their descendants, so that like is joined to like.

And he traces the branches of the pole (quṭb) Sidi Yahya back

to Sidi Idris, of original nobility,

to his father Idris, of glory and eminence,

to the excellent Abdullah, of merit and justice,

to al-Hasan the excellent, al-Muthanna, who rose to

the summits of might, of divine enabling, of forbearance and of sound judgement,

to al-Hasan the grandson, son of Haydara the well-pleasing,

through Fatimah al-Zahra, to the master of the messengers —

upon him be God's blessings without ceasing, and upon his family,

and the purest peace, joining the branch to the root.

Written by Muhammad al-Hasan ibn al-Dedew.

flags.context: the title of the book being commended
options: The Genealogical Tree of the Idrisids of Sidi Yahya
The Idrisid Lineage of Sidi Yahya
leave the Arabic title untranslated and transliterate it
flags.note: A book title. The rendering given is descriptive; the book's own published English title, if it has one, should be used instead once the Sheikh's office can confirm it. The genitive construction is loose in the Arabic and could also mean 'the Idrisid tree, [namely that of] Sidi Yahya'.

A Mauritanian tribal or place name with no settled English transliteration; the vocalisation cannot be fixed from the unpointed text. Needs the Sheikh's office to confirm both the vocalisation and whether the referent is a lineage or a locality.

flags.context: و للقطب سيدي يحي ينهي فروعه
flags.note: quṭb is a Sufi rank denoting the figure held to be the spiritual axis of his age. It is a term of art with a doctrinal history and is not in the glossary; it should be added rather than rendered ad hoc, since an over-plain English rendering would erase the technical claim the poem makes.

flags.context: إلى الحسن الندب المثنى من ارتقى
options: al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan, known as al-Muthanna ('the second')
the excellent al-Hasan, the second of that name
flags.note: المثنى is the epithet of al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, distinguishing him from his father. Whether to render the epithet or gloss it affects how legible the chain is to an English reader; nothing has been added to the chain itself.

flags.context: إلى الحسن السبط ابن حيدرة الرضا
options: son of Haydara (Ali ibn Abi Talib), with whom God is pleased
son of the lion, the well-pleasing one
flags.note: حيدرة is a by-name of Ali ibn Abi Talib, meaning 'lion'. Left as the name, since glossing it as 'the lion' would obscure that a person is being named. Whether الرضا is an epithet of Ali or the formula raḍiya Allāh ʿanhu compressed for the metre is not certain from the text.

translator_notes: Verse (nazm). Style guide section 4 requires verse to be rendered as prose in italics with the Arabic retained in the bilingual pane; body_ar carries the Arabic line for line and body_en keeps the same line division so the two panes align. No rhymed English has been attempted.

Genre: poetry, filed by the site under الشعر (Poetry). The schema's type list has no value for poetry, so 'article' has been used; the genre is recorded here and in section/category. The schema should gain a poetry type.
تقريظ is the classical genre of a commendatory notice written for a book, usually in verse; rendered 'commendation' rather than 'review', which would suggest evaluation.

The closing genealogy traces Sidi Yahya to al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan (al-Muthanna), to al-Hasan the grandson of the Prophet, to Ali ibn Abi Talib (Haydara) and Fatimah al-Zahra. The chain is the poem's substance and has been kept name for name, with none added and none dropped.
A recording is linked on this record as well as the text; unlike the audio-only records in this range, the written text here is complete in itself.
No ruling of any kind is given, so the five-rulings mapping of style guide section 3 is not engaged.

The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload/publication stamp, not the date on which the Sheikh gave the answer. Records across this range carry timestamps clustered minutes apart on the same day (e.g. 1275-1278 at 09:51/09:53/09:54/09:55 on 7 March 2022), which is the signature of a batch upload. date_is_cms_upload is therefore set true throughout.
